subject: Re: Aligning regional failover premiums with on-call retainer options
messages:
From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@brightline.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Regional failover premium + retainer credits — quick sync?

Hi Rachel / Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving toward a Dedicated deployment and want to lock down economics for failover behavior across regions. Two quick asks from procurement and engineering: 

- Brightline runs mission-critical traffic across us-west and eu-west; they want a clear premium for guaranteed failover (i.e., cross-region cold-start capacity + DR routing) — procurement expects this to be a line item.
- Simultaneously, they're evaluating an annual on-call retainer (hours-based) and asked if Redwood will discount the failover premium in exchange for a multi-region retainer commitment.

Can you share an exchange framework (what discount in return for which retainer level, and whether seat swaps or credits apply)? Procurement would like a short matrix to take to their CFO.

Attached: example network topology (for context).

Appreciate a brief proposal by COB Monday if possible.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Wu
Sourcing Manager, Brightline Systems
[Attachment: brightline_topology.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@brightline.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional failover premium + retainer credits — quick sync?

Hi Elaine — great question and happy to outline options. High level: we can structure a trade where Brightline commits to an annual on-call retainer (hours + response SLAs) and we apply a sliding discount to the region-failover premium and to certain on-demand burst usage during failover events. Key points below — I'll loop Jonas for the numbers.

Option summary (draft):
- Bronze retainer: 200 hours/year, 24/7 triage window, 5-day response SLA for non-critical events -> 10% reduction to failover premium, no seat swaps.
- Silver retainer: 600 hours/year, 24/7 triage + 2-hour critical response SLA -> 25% reduction, plus 10 credits for short-term seat swaps during maintenance windows.
- Gold retainer: 1200 hours/year, 24/7 + dedicated on-call roster and 1-hour critical response SLA -> 40% reduction, 25 seat-swap credits, and waived cross-region data egress for DR failovers up to agreed levels.

Open items for procurement: how Brightline measures a ‘failover event’ (thresholds), whether credits roll over, and whether discounts apply to committed capacity only or both committed + burst.

Jonas — attaching a pricing matrix and proposed term sheet (v3) for your review. Naomi — can you confirm any constraints around seat-swap allocation (legal/ops)?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-retainer-term-sheet.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Regional failover premium + retainer credits — quick sync?

Forwarding my working numbers — see attached pricing_matrix_v3. Notes inline below.

> Pricing matrix highlights (internal):
> - Failover premium baseline: 18% of committed capacity cost for same-region cold-start capacity; 30% for cross-region guaranteed capacity when warm standby is requested.
> - Proposed exchange: each 200 annual retainer hours -> 10 percentage points off the failover premium (cumulative, capped at 40%).
> - Seat-swap credits: defined as 8-hour temporary entitlement to move a reserved slot between teams/regions; credits are non-transferable outside of the contracted account.
> - Billing treatment: discounts apply to committed capacity charges only; burst usage billed at standard on-demand rates but with a reduced multiplier during an approved failover event (0.75x of on-demand).
> - Legal: require explicit event definition in SOW and an audit window to validate a failover claim.

Attachment: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet) — contains per-region sample calculations and a templated SOW clause.

Jonas
Senior Pricing Analyst, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@brightline.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional failover premium + retainer credits — quick sync?

Rachel / Jonas — thanks, this is exactly what procurement needed. Brightline's CFO prefers the Silver path with a tweak: make the seat-swap credits transferrable within our org (we operate several BU-level accounts). Also want an explicit clause limiting qualifying failover events to those where traffic normally exceeds 70% of baseline across the primary region for 10+ consecutive minutes.

If you can update the term-sheet to reflect transferable seat-swap credits (internal transfer only) and add the event definition above, we can route this through DocuSign this week. Can you send a DocuSign link and final SOW addendum?

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Wu
Sourcing Manager, Brightline Systems
